title: Laminar flow in a helical pipe
summary: Steady laminar flow through four turns of a helical coil (the SIET coil: 12.53 mm tube, 1 m helix diameter, 0.8 m pitch), meshed by hexmesh along a spline through the helix.  It checks that the friction factor converges as the mesh is refined and lands within 5 % of Ito's correlation.  Two of the three Reynolds numbers are done on the finest mesh; the last one, Re 3000, needs 9 to 12 hours on 4 cores and several GB of memory, which our one desktop can't spare.

hexmesh.note: clone this tag with git clone --branch, as in the five commands: the mesh check needs the same meshing code as ours

gmsh.note: the version pip installs with hexmesh is fine: our test level's mesh check gives the same fingerprint with gmsh 4.12.1 and 4.15.2

re3000_n24.title: Re 3000 on the finest mesh (nang 24)
re3000_n24.what: The run first solves the next-coarser mesh (nang 16, 0.8 million cells) and starts the fine one (2.7 million cells) from its mapped result, which shortens the fine solve.  Both stop when the solver converges (at most 5000 steps); the results are saved every 50 steps.

cores.label: cores (MPI processes)
cores.how: our runs of this level at Re 1800 and 2400 used 4 processes on one 8-core desktop; any count from 1 works, more is faster

wall_time.label: wall time at 4 cores
wall_time.how: an upper bound from a measured start of this level at 4 processes (desktop, 2026-11-10): the coarse solve converged in 788 steps at 5.4 s/step (1.2 h); the first 50 fine steps took 70 s/step, while other jobs shared the machine; the fine solve's steps are scaled from Re 2400 (398 fine steps after 563 coarse ones) to about 560, so 10.8 h.  At Re 2400's fine rate (51 s/step) it would be about 9 h

prepare_time.label: time to prepare (one core, no MPI)
prepare_time.how: making, converting and checking both meshes and preparing the coarse start: 27 min (desktop, 2026-11-10)

peak_memory.label: peak memory
peak_memory.how: the run's processes and Docker containers summed, sampled every 2 s (desktop, 2026-11-10): 2.6 GB preparing, 1.1 GB in the coarse solve, 1.8 GB mapping, 3.6 GB in the fine solve at 4 processes

peak_disk.label: peak disk
peak_disk.how: the run's directory, sampled every 20 s through preparing, the coarse solve, mapping and the first fine chunk (desktop, 2026-11-10): 2.4 GB at most; later chunks keep only the latest result, so it stays there

cells.label: cells
cells.how: the fine mesh's exact count (the coarse start has 803328)
